components.name: pqscan
components.description: Post-quantum crypto scanner for Python projects (research prototype)

properties.name: pqscan:disclaimer
properties.value: Migration guidance only; does not establish that a migrated system is secure, compliant or quantum-safe.

properties.name: pqscan:rationale
properties.value: Evidence tier T0 is below the policy threshold T2: the receiver is not resolved to a key object and no algorithm-specific argument is visible. Inferred role (not acted on): SIGN.

properties.name: pqscan:reason
properties.value: operation .sign() -> SIGN; receiver unresolved (untyped parameter); arguments: no parameters

properties.name: pqscan:rationale
properties.value: Role cannot be determined: key material (RSA) reaches consumers of 2 families (PKE, SIG); the role depends on which path runs, so it is not statically determinable. Possible roles: PK_DECRYPT, SIGN, VERIFY. No single target is justified.

properties.name: pqscan:reason
properties.value: key material (RSA) reaches consumers of 2 families (PKE, SIG); the role depends on which path runs, so it is not statically determinable

properties.name: pqscan:target
properties.value: ML-DSA (FIPS 204); SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) where its size/speed trade-offs are acceptable

properties.name: pqscan:rationale
properties.value: RSA signing is deprecated after 2030 and disallowed after 2035 (NIST IR 8547 Table 2). Migrate signing to ML-DSA (FIPS 204); dual/hybrid signatures are a transitional option; verifiers and certificate chains must be able to accept ML-DSA before signers switch.

properties.name: pqscan:reason
properties.value: operation .sign() -> SIGN; receiver resolved: pyca:RSA:private:generated; arguments: padding=PKCS1v15, hash=SHA256; the key may also come from an untyped parameter, or its origin is consumed by another role family or has conflicting consumers, so the tier is capped at T2

properties.name: pqscan:parameterSet
properties.value: ML-DSA-65 (category 3) by default; ML-DSA-44 only with an RBG of >= 192-bit strength if category 2 is required; ML-DSA-87 for category 5

properties.name: pqscan:target
properties.value: Redesign as KEM + KDF + AEAD (KEM/DEM, SP 800-227 Secs. 5.2.1, 4.3); not a drop-in replacement for encrypt/decrypt

properties.name: pqscan:rationale
properties.value: RSA public-key decryption / key unwrapping has no drop-in PQC replacement. Redesign as KEM + KDF + AEAD (SP 800-227 Secs. 5.2.1, 4.3), decapsulation side: decapsulate with the ML-KEM decapsulation key, derive the content key from the shared secret (FIPS 203 Sec. 3.3), and decrypt with an AEAD. The existing decrypt(ciphertext) call shape cannot be preserved.

properties.name: pqscan:reason
properties.value: operation .decrypt() -> PK_DECRYPT; receiver resolved: pyca:RSA:private:generated; arguments: padding=OAEP, hash=SHA256; the key may also come from an untyped parameter, or its origin is consumed by another role family or has conflicting consumers, so the tier is capped at T2

properties.name: pqscan:parameterSet
properties.value: ML-KEM-768 (NIST IR 8547 default recommendation) with an approved KDF and AEAD

properties.name: pqscan:target
properties.value: ML-DSA (FIPS 204); SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) where its size/speed trade-offs are acceptable

properties.name: pqscan:rationale
properties.value: ECDSA/ECDH (elliptic-curve) signing is deprecated after 2030 and disallowed after 2035 (NIST IR 8547 Table 2). Migrate signing to ML-DSA (FIPS 204); dual/hybrid signatures are a transitional option; verifiers and certificate chains must be able to accept ML-DSA before signers switch.

properties.name: pqscan:rationale
properties.value: RSA public-key encryption / key transport (PKCS#1 v1.5, OAEP) has no drop-in PQC replacement. Redesign as KEM + KDF + AEAD (SP 800-227 Secs. 5.2.1, 4.3): the sender encapsulates to the recipient's authenticated ML-KEM key, derives the content key from the shared secret (FIPS 203 Sec. 3.3), and encrypts with an AEAD. The existing encrypt(data) call shape cannot be preserved.

properties.name: pqscan:target
properties.value: ML-KEM-based key-establishment redesign (FIPS 203, SP 800-227); PQ/T hybrid with the existing scheme through an approved combiner is an acceptable transitional design

properties.name: pqscan:rationale
properties.value: X25519 key establishment is deprecated after 2030 and disallowed after 2035 (NIST IR 8547 Table 4) and is exposed to harvest-now-decrypt-later. Redesign around ML-KEM (FIPS 203; ML-KEM-768 recommended by NIST IR 8547) per SP 800-227; a PQ/T hybrid with the existing scheme via an approved combiner (SP 800-227 Sec. 4.6) is an acceptable transitional design. ML-KEM uses encapsulate/decapsulate, not a symmetric exchange(peer) call.

properties.name: pqscan:target
properties.value: ML-DSA (FIPS 204); SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) where its size/speed trade-offs are acceptable

properties.name: pqscan:rationale
properties.value: Add ML-DSA (FIPS 204) verification so that migrated signers can be accepted. NIST IR 8547 defines 'legacy use' as processing already-protected data such as verifying an existing signature; whether RSA verification of already-issued signatures keeps that status after 2035 is set by SP 800-131A (to be revised). Retain legacy verification only for already-issued signatures; do not accept new RSA signatures after the transition.
